transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm not overreacting by coming in, but I'm here because... well, I've barely been sleeping lately. 

It started after a warehouse inspection I had to do for work. There was an incident—a blast—and... I don't know, I just lie in bed replaying bits of it in my head. I really try to just shut it off, but when I actually do manage to drift off, I wake up all sweaty and wide awake, almost like I’m right back near that blast. 

I'm sorry, I know it probably sounds a bit dramatic, and I'm sure it's just my brain overworking, but... does that make sense? Is that something you see people for here?
Since the blast, have you found yourself avoiding certain places, people, or activities that remind you of what happened?

Um, well... maybe just a little bit? I'm really trying my best not to let it affect my work, I promise. But... I guess I have been sort of avoiding the file for that specific warehouse. And, um, if a call comes in about any of our other industrial accounts, I've... I've kind of been letting them go to voicemail. 

I know that's not very professional, and I feel awful about it, but honestly, even just opening emails about those types of accounts makes my stomach completely drop. I mean, I always plan to get back to them! I just... I hope that doesn't make me sound terrible. Is it... is it normal to want to push those things away right now?
Since the blast, have you been feeling ongoing fear, guilt, or anger, especially when you think about what happened?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I wouldn't say I'm feeling angry or anything like that. I try really hard to keep a positive attitude, you know? 

I guess... maybe I feel a tiny bit bad sometimes? Just because I'm not doing my job as well as I usually do right now, and I hate letting my team down. But it's not like a deep, dark guilt or anything! And fear... well, I'm a little jumpy, sure, but I wouldn't say I'm walking around terrified all day. 

I'm mostly just... trying to move past it. I hope it's okay that I don't have a lot of those intense feelings you mentioned. Is it a good sign that I'm not feeling angry about it?
Since the blast, have you had any moments where you felt intense fear, guilt, or anger come up unexpectedly when reminded of the event, even if just slightly?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I definitely don't want to sound like I'm hiding anything, but... no, I haven't really had any sudden bursts of anger or, you know, intense fear like that. 

Like I said, I feel a little bad about the work stuff, but it's really just a mild thing because I want to be doing a good job. I'm really trying to keep things steady and not let myself get all worked up. I hope that's the right way to handle it? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information... but yeah, no big unexpected waves of those feelings. Does that make sense?
